Description: Subjects and possessives are attached directly to the verb or noun.
Emotions and physical needs are locations resting on you.
Key Rule: Attach the -la suffix to a pronoun to indicate this state.
Context/Note: Emotions/needs are not things you are, but places you occupy.

Description: Turns a base concept or action verb into a physical output radiating from a body.
Key Rule: Use for things a body involuntarily produces (heat, chill, scent, visual presence, flavor, sound).
Context/Note: Solves Noun vs. Verb ambiguity (e.g., osh = to smell; oshet = the scent produced).

Concept: Plural / Intensity by Doubling First Syllable
Description: Doubling the first syllable indicates multiple instances, high intensity, or relentless action.
Key Rule: If the syllable has double of the same consonants, only use the first one.
Context/Note: E.g., vek -> vevek (deep/multiple cuts); ikku -> ikikku (relentless climaxing).

Description: The naked verb becomes the command
Verb prefixes/suffixes always prioritize the anatomy being stimulated, regardless of who is doing it.
Key Rule: If a player sucks a monster's cock, the monster still calls it deh-glim (cock-suck) because their deh is the focus.
Context/Note: Keeps the linguistic focus aggressively centered on the monster's physical experience and dominance.

Description: Do not use a connective word for "is" or "are".
Key Rule: Slam nouns, states, and modifiers directly into each other.
Context/Note: Creates a blunt, undeniable biological fact.

Key Rule: Omit articles unless absolutely necessary for clarity.
Context/Note: Focuses on the core essence of the nouns.

Key Rule: State data as absolute physical laws.
Context/Note: Removes social softeners to state facts as absolute.

Description: Added to the end of a sentence to turn a statement of physical fact into a question, or a direct, guttural challenge.
Key Rule: Place at the end of the sentence after the statement.
Context/Note: E.g., Jiten-mi, he? (You steal from me, eh?)

Description: A hard boolean false. Used after a comma to brutally revoke or negate the preceding statement.
Key Rule: Place after a comma following the statement to negate.
Context/Note: E.g., Mekkan-ni fim, inji. (Your body is wet, false. / You are not wet.)

Description: Attached directly to a verb to change a neutral, biological action into an act of malice, harm, or parasitic intent.
Key Rule: Prefix attaches directly to the verb root.
Context/Note: E.g., ten -> jiten (steal); vek -> jivek (torture); mjis -> jimjis (force-breed / parasitic insemination).

Description: Turns a raw concept or action into a tangible, defined, harvestable object.
Key Rule: Suffix attaches directly to the root word.
Context/Note: E.g., mekk -> mekkan (the physical body); mjis -> mjisan (the physical seed / harvestable milt).

Description: Turns a root concept into an overwhelming systemic state of being, roughly '-without any hope of return'.
Key Rule: Suffix attaches directly to the root word. Often used for mind-shatter or pleasure-coma mechanics.
Context/Note: E.g., bolk -> bolkep (madness); ash -> ashep (euphoric bliss); fim -> fimep (in estrus).

Description: The entity who does / the vessel of the action.
Key Rule: Suffix attaches directly to the root verb to create an entity/vessel.
Context/Note: Attach to a verb to indicate that the entity/vessel is "the one who [verbs]". Jitengut (thief / the one who maliciously takes), or deh-glimgut (cocksucker).
